This vignette is precomputed --- it downloads several hundred megabytes --- but
the code is what you would run.


``` r
library(canstreet)
library(dplyr)
```

## Set a cache path

A national vintage is 200–350 MB compressed and about 2.2 million segments, so
`canstreet` caches the archives and the harmonized database. The cache path is
read from the `CANSTREET_CACHE_PATH` environment variable, which
`set_canstreet_cache_path()` sets. With `install = TRUE` it also writes it to
`.Renviron`, so it is available in all future sessions and does not need to be
set again.


``` r
set_canstreet_cache_path("~/data/canstreet", install = TRUE)
```


## Available vintages


``` r
list_road_network_vintages() |>
  select(vintage, product, coverage, source_crs, imported)
#> # A tibble: 28 × 5
#>    vintage product coverage source_crs imported
#>      <int> <chr>   <chr>    <chr>      <lgl>   
#>  1    1971 AMF     urban    EPSG:4267  TRUE    
#>  2    1976 AMF     urban    EPSG:4267  TRUE    
#>  3    1981 AMF     urban    EPSG:4267  TRUE    
#>  4    1986 AMF     urban    EPSG:4267  TRUE    
#>  5    1991 SNF     urban    EPSG:4267  TRUE    
#>  6    1996 SNF     urban    EPSG:4267  TRUE    
#>  7    2001 RNF     national EPSG:4269  TRUE    
#>  8    2005 RNF     national EPSG:4269  TRUE    
#>  9    2006 RNF     national EPSG:4269  TRUE    
#> 10    2007 RNF     national EPSG:4269  FALSE   
#> # ℹ 18 more rows
```

The 1971 to 1986 Area Master Files and the 1991 and 1996 Street Network Files
cover urban areas only; everything from 2001 on is national. From 2005 on the
files are annual; before that there is one per census year.

## Getting a vintage

`get_road_network()` is the universal way to access the road network data for a
given vintage: if needed it fetches the data and parses it into a local
database, and it hands back a lazy DuckDB table.


``` r
roads <- get_road_network(2021)
roads
#> # A query:  ?? x 24
#> # Database: DuckDB 1.5.6 [jens@Darwin 27.0.0:R 4.6.0//Users/jens/data/canstreet/canstreet.duckdb]
```

Once downloaded, connecting to the database is instant. Chain `dplyr`
operations before calling `collect()` so that they run in DuckDB, which keeps
memory use low and execution fast.


``` r
roads |>
  filter(!is.na(pruid_l)) |>
  group_by(pruid_l) |>
  summarize(segments = n(), km = round(sum(len_m, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000)) |>
  arrange(desc(km)) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 13 × 3
#>    pruid_l segments     km
#>    <chr>      <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1 47        223061 237403
#>  2 35        570216 229710
#>  3 48        369662 214914
#>  4 24        446796 148103

#>  9 10         54109  24947
#> 10 60          5712   8849
#> 11 11         16415   6941
#> 12 61          5751   6234
#> 13 62          3227    864
```

## Spatial filters

Pass any `sf`, `sfc` or `bbox` object as `within`. Over a single vintage the
filter uses that vintage's R-tree index, so it stays fast on a national file.
`collect_road_network()` then materializes the result as `sf`.


``` r
bbox <- sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = -123.15, ymin = 49.26, xmax = -123.09,
                      ymax = 49.29), crs = 4326)

downtown <- get_road_network(2021, within = bbox) |>
  collect_road_network()

downtown |> select(name, type, af_l, at_l, csdname_l)
#> Simple feature collection with 2099 features and 5 fields
#> Geometry type: LINESTRING
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 4015724 ymin: 2004073 xmax: 4021033 ymax: 2008953
#> Projected CRS: NAD83 / Statistics Canada Lambert
#> # A tibble: 2,099 × 6
#>    name          type   af_l  at_l csdname_l                                geom
#>    <chr>         <chr> <int> <int> <chr>                        <LINESTRING [m]>
#>  1 11th          AVE     605   675 Vancouver  (4019577 2004160, 4019699 2004093)
#>  2 Carolina      ST     2706  2724 Vancouver (4019577 2004160, 4019553 2004116,…

```


``` r
plot(sf::st_geometry(downtown), col = "grey30", lwd = 0.6)
```

<div class="figure">
<img src="canstreet-plot-1.png" alt="Street segments in downtown Vancouver, 2021" width="100%" />
<p class="caption">plot of chunk plot</p>
</div>

Geometry is always converted to and stored in EPSG:3347 (NAD83 / Statistics Canada Lambert), so `len_m`
is metres for every vintage. `collect_road_network()` reprojects on request:


``` r
get_road_network(2021, within = bbox) |>
  collect_road_network(crs = 4326) |>
  sf::st_crs() |>
  (\(x) x$epsg)()
#> [1] 4326
```

## Comparing vintages

Calling `get_road_network()` with several vintages hands back one lazy table
with the vintages stacked, so a query runs over all of them at once.


``` r
get_road_network(c(1971, 1976, 1981, 1986, 1991, 1996, 2001, 2006, 2011, 2016,
                   2021)) |>
  group_by(vintage) |>
  summarize(segments = n(), km = round(sum(len_m, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000)) |>
  arrange(vintage) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 11 × 3
#>    vintage segments      km
#>      <int>    <dbl>   <dbl>
#>  1    1971   215399   31882
#>  2    1976   431844   65709
#>  3    1981   529158   80100
#>  4    1986   909065  135232
#>  5    1991   599625  160778
#>  6    1996   629574  167238
#>  7    2001  2053112 1736503
#>  8    2006  1869564 1326099
#>  9    2011  1973932 1326662
#> 10    2016  2163058 1157951
#> 11    2021  2242117 1170167
```

Nothing before 2001 is national, and the Area Master Files grow mostly by
covering more places (34 municipal files in 1971, 194 in 1986), so most of the rise
to 1996 is due to expanding coverage. Segment counts do not compare across
products either. 1986 holds more segments than 1991 over fewer kilometres
because an Area Master File segment is a single block face. And not every
segment is a road: over a third of 1986's arcs are shorelines, boundaries and
railways, and 2001's extra 400,000 km is census boundary topology.
Setting `roads_only = TRUE` drops both. The 2006–2021 drop is in the source data, not
the import. 2006 carries far more very long arcs, which later releases split,
reclassified or dropped.


``` r
get_road_network(c(2006, 2021)) |>
  filter(len_m > 5000) |>
  group_by(vintage) |>
  summarize(long_arcs = n(), km = round(sum(len_m, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000)) |>
  collect()
#> # A tibble: 2 × 3
#>   vintage long_arcs     km
#>     <int>     <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1    2006     22486 206308
#> 2    2021     13055 120875
```

Identifiers are not stable across vintages, so comparing years
is done by matching on geometry only. `build_temporal_network()` does that and writes one
table in which each segment carries the years it is present in. For details,
see the vignette on temporal matching, `vignette("canstreet-temporal")`.

## The harmonized schema

Every vintage maps onto the same columns; where a vintage does not carry a
column, its values are `NA`.


``` r
canstreet_schema()
#> # A tibble: 24 × 3
#>    column      type    source_columns                         
#>    <chr>       <chr>   <chr>                                  
#>  1 vintage     INTEGER (reference year)                       
#>  2 source_file VARCHAR (name of the source archive member)    
#>  3 source_id   VARCHAR NGD_UID, NGDUID, NGD_ID, RB_UID, ARC_ID
#>  4 name        VARCHAR NAME                                   
#>  5 type        VARCHAR TYPE                                   
#>  6 dir         VARCHAR DIR, DIRECTION                         
#>  7 af_l        INTEGER AFL_VAL, ADDR_FM_LE, ADDR_FM_LEFT      
#>  8 at_l        INTEGER ATL_VAL, ADDR_TO_LE, ADDR_TO_LEFT      
#>  9 af_r        INTEGER AFR_VAL, ADDR_FM_RG, ADDR_FM_RGHT      
#> 10 at_r        INTEGER ATR_VAL, ADDR_TO_RG, ADDR_TO_RGHT      
#> # ℹ 14 more rows
```

Source spellings differ by vintage — `arc_id` in 1991/1996, `RB_UID` in
2001–2010, `NGD_UID` from 2011, `NGDUID` in 2016/2017 — and the importer
resolves each by alias.

## Exporting

Other systems such as Python or QGIS can read the same DuckDB file; its local
path is the `path` element of `get_road_network_database()`. There is also an
`export_road_network()` convenience function that exports the data to
GeoParquet with the CRS in its metadata:


``` r
get_road_network(2021, within = bbox) |>
  export_road_network("vancouver_2021.parquet")
```

## Managing the cache

Several convenience functions help manage the cache.


``` r
list_canstreet_cache()
#> # A tibble: 12 × 6
#>    vintage n_segments n_archives raw_mb imported_at              package_version
#>      <int>      <int>      <int>  <dbl> <chr>                    <chr>          
#>  1    1971     215399          1   10.2 2026-10-01T14:26:44-0700 0.0.1          
#>  2    1976     431844          1   17.4 2026-10-01T14:07:02-0700 0.0.0.9000     
#>  3    1981     529158          1   19.7 2026-10-01T14:07:28-0700 0.0.0.9000     
#>  4    1986     909065          1   27.7 2026-10-01T14:27:28-0700 0.0.1          
#>  5    1991     599625         51   72.5 2026-08-29T12:49:40-0700 0.0.0.9000     
#>  6    1996     629574         50   70.5 2026-08-29T12:46:01-0700 0.0.0.9000     
#>  7    2001    2053112          1  250   2026-08-29T11:15:39-0700 0.0.0.9000     
#>  8    2005    1864299          1  254.  2026-10-01T17:30:49-0700 0.0.1          
#>  9    2006    1869564          1  219.  2026-08-28T18:57:14-0700 0.0.0.9000     
#> 10    2011    1973932          1  334.  2026-08-28T18:57:40-0700 0.0.0.9000     
#> 11    2016    2163058          1  327.  2026-08-28T18:58:07-0700 0.0.0.9000     
#> 12    2021    2242117          1  310.  2026-08-28T18:58:34-0700 0.0.0.9000
```

`remove_canstreet_cache(vintage)` drops a vintage's table and keeps its
archives, so it can be re-imported without downloading again; pass
`keep_raw = FALSE` to delete those too.
